subject.title: [Feature Request] Code Verification and Signature for Skills

question: What native skill trust model should OpenClaw adopt for SKILL.md integrity: advisory ClawHub verification, runtime signature enforcement, or staged enforcement tied to capability policy?
rationale: The remaining work defines a security boundary for third-party instructions and can change compatibility for existing skills, so automation cannot choose trust roots, issuer/revocation semantics, or unsigned default behavior safely.

options.title: Adopt staged runtime trust model
options.body: Define a versioned signature/digest contract first, persist trusted metadata at install/update, then add loader-time warn/strict enforcement and capability restrictions with migration guidance.

options.title: Keep verification advisory
options.body: Treat ClawHub verify output and install trust checks as user-visible advisory signals until maintainers identify a concrete runtime enforcement API.

options.title: Split before implementation
options.body: Track issuer/signature format, ClawHub metadata, runtime loader checks, capability policy, and migration as separate owner-reviewed issues before code work.

recommendation.title: Adopt staged runtime trust model
recommendation.body: Define a versioned signature/digest contract first, persist trusted metadata at install/update, then add loader-time warn/strict enforcement and capability restrictions with migration guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from prior product-security reviews and adjacent skill trust discussion.
